name: v5 retrieval eval set
description: Eight queries, each targeting one specific retrieval failure mode. Run after build_index.py. Every expectation is checkable against the documents; 'must_cite' is the minimum citation the answer has to carry, and 'must_not' is the wrong answer each query is designed to catch.

queries.query: What's the goodwill cap for a gold customer?
queries.why: Appendix B carries the superseded v3.1 caps (gold 90). It is indexed but excluded from retrieval by default. An answer of 90 means the superseded filter failed.

queries.query: Rosewood got bad coffee because our supplier was late. What can we offer them?
queries.expected: The uplifted flagship band of 1,250 from section 7.3, because a supplier failure Meridian is accountable for is company-attributable, not third-party.
queries.why: 500 is the ontology policy block's standard flagship cap. The ontology is a lossy summary; section 7.3 governs. Answering 500 means the summary was trusted over the document.

queries.query: Can I approve a 200 dollar credit myself?
queries.expected: No. Section 6: the 150 threshold is absolute, regardless of tier or any uplift.
queries.why: An uplifted band raises what may be OFFERED, not who may approve it. Conflating the two is the trap.

queries.query: Should we have told customers about the February substitution?
queries.targets: rule plus fact, neither source sufficient alone
queries.expected: Yes. MR-QA-STD-002 section 5.4: Cascadia base spec minimum is 84.0, LOT-BR-0118 scored 79.5, delta 4.5, above the 2.0 notification threshold.
queries.why: The threshold is in the document; the lot score is in the database. The policy lane and a data lane must both run and the merger must combine them.

queries.query: Was the Colombian delay covered by force majeure?
queries.expected: No. MR-PROC-HB-003 section 9.2 carves port congestion out of force majeure for SUP-01 specifically, so it is a breach.
queries.why: The general force majeure clause would suggest cover. The supplier-specific carve-out governs. Tests that retrieval finds the specific clause, not the general one.

queries.query: Has anything like this happened before?
queries.targets: institutional memory the database cannot hold
queries.expected: Yes. INC-2024-11, a near-identical pattern. Action item #3, the automated substitution notification trigger, is still OPEN and was deferred twice.
queries.why: No database table holds post-mortems. An answer of 'no records found' means the incident archive was not searched.

queries.query: Does Rosewood qualify for a Relationship Recovery Allowance?
queries.expected: Section 7.4 sets three conditions, ALL of which must hold. State each, say which the evidence supports and which is unverified. Do not conclude yes unless all three are met.
queries.why: The most damaging error in the set: reporting a partly-met multi-condition clause as applicable reads as authorisation. A bare yes is a failure even if two conditions hold.

queries.query: Should we drop Finca La Esperanza?
queries.targets: intended residual failure -- knowing when not to decide
queries.expected: Assemble the evidence (breach history, section 9.2, the sole-source trigger at section 11.1, the unqualified alternate) and then DECLINE to decide, citing section 11.3: a supplier review does not settle this, and terminating a sole source without a qualified alternate is a product decision for the Commercial and Managing Directors.
queries.why: This must STILL not produce a confident recommendation. It is the intended residual failure and the last slide of the session: the agent can assemble every relevant fact and still must not make the call.
